correctness.rationale: A nonzero ideal has exactly one generator with a>0, b>=0. For h=floor(sqrt(k)), b<h contributes at most h^2 and b=h contributes at most floor(sqrt(k-h^2))<=k-h^2; hence A(k)<=k. For s=n+1>2 the ordered-pair max-norm series U_s converges by coefficient comparison with 2Z(s-1)-Z(s). Dividing both ideals by their unique gcd gives a coprime pair, with multiplicative max norm under the common factor; thus U_s=Z(s)T_s. The circle estimate gives W_n(y)~pi*y^(n+1)/(4(n+1)) by partial summation. The bound W_n(y)<=y^(n+1), also below y=1, provides summable domination by the coprime max-norm weights after scaling the exact gcd decomposition by X^(n+1). Dividing the limit by A(floor X)^2/X^2 -> pi^2/16 gives the claimed coefficient, including n=2. Norm counts at 1,2,3,4 are 1,1,0,1, so the max-norm coefficient at k=4 is 5 versus 7 in the conjectured series. All other coefficient differences are nonnegative, giving the exact stated lower bound. This proves the claim for each fixed n, not a growing-exponent estimate. The supplied checker and verification note describe bounded corroboration, not the limiting argument.
